title: Body in a recording medium: the probe's witness geometry

key_results.statement: Block form of the combined contract: $C=\sum_{h,\beta}\Pi_{h\beta}\otimes(K_h+B_\beta)$ with the mutually orthogonal projectors $\Pi_{h\beta}=\lvert h\rangle\langle h\rvert_p\otimes\lvert\beta\rangle\langle\beta\rvert_b$, $\sum_{h,\beta}\Pi_{h\beta}=\mathbb 1_p\otimes\mathbb 1_b$.
Exact evolution operator for every $\lambda$: $e^{-\mathrm iC\lambda}=\sum_{h,\beta}\Pi_{h\beta}\otimes e^{-\mathrm i(K_h+B_\beta)\lambda}$, although the two contracts need not commute.

Exact state for every $\lambda\ge0$: $\lvert\Psi(\lambda)\rangle=\sum_h\phi_h\,\lvert h\rangle_p\otimes\lvert\beta_0\rangle_b\otimes e^{-\mathrm i(K_h+B_{\beta_0})\lambda}\lvert\chi\rangle_c$; the probe weights $p_h=\lvert\phi_h\rvert^2$ do not depend on $\lambda$.

The body stays at the single place $\beta_0$ for every $\lambda$: its view is $V_{\{b\}}(\Psi(\lambda))=\lvert\beta_0\rangle\langle\beta_0\rvert$ and $p_b(\beta)=\delta_{\beta\beta_0}$, and it never becomes correlated with $p$ or $c$.

Witness data of the probe with the body at $\beta_0$, exact for every $\lambda$: $W^{(\beta_0)}(h,h';\lambda)=\bigl\lvert\langle\chi\vert e^{\mathrm i(K_{h'}+B_{\beta_0})\lambda}e^{-\mathrm i(K_h+B_{\beta_0})\lambda}\vert\chi\rangle\bigr\rvert^2$; for $B_{\beta_0}=0$ it is (5.6).

If $[B_{\beta_0},K_h]=[B_{\beta_0},K_{h'}]=0$, then $W^{(\beta_0)}(h,h';\lambda)=W(h,h';\lambda)$ of (5.6) for every $\lambda\ge0$, and even the overlap is body-free; in particular $B_{\beta_0}\propto\mathbb 1$ has no effect.

As $\lambda\to0^+$, with $D=K_h-K_{h'}$: $W^{(\beta_0)}(h,h';\lambda)=1-\lambda^2\operatorname{Var}_\chi(D)+\lambda^3c_3^{(\beta_0)}(h,h')+O(\lambda^4)$; the $\lambda^2$ term does not depend on the body.

$c_3^{(\beta_0)}(h,h')=\operatorname{Im}\langle\chi\vert(K_{h'}+B_{\beta_0})\tilde D^2\vert\chi\rangle$ with $\tilde D=D-\langle D\rangle$; $K_{h'}$ may be replaced by $K_h$, so $c_3^{(\beta_0)}$ is symmetric in $h,h'$.

Body-dependent part of the third-order coefficient: $c_3^{(\beta_0)}=c_3^{(0)}+\operatorname{Im}\langle\chi\vert B_{\beta_0}\tilde D^2\vert\chi\rangle$, where $c_3^{(0)}=\operatorname{Im}\langle\chi\vert K_{h'}\tilde D^2\vert\chi\rangle$ is the body-free coefficient of (5.6) and $\operatorname{Im}\langle\chi\vert B_{\beta_0}\tilde D^2\vert\chi\rangle=\langle\chi\vert[B_{\beta_0},\tilde D^2]\vert\chi\rangle/(2\mathrm i)$.

For $d_0(h,h')>0$, as $\lambda\to0^+$: $\alpha^{(\beta_0)}(h,h';\lambda)=\lambda d_0(h,h')+\lambda^2\alpha_2^{(\beta_0)}(h,h')+O(\lambda^3)$ with $\alpha_2^{(\beta_0)}=-c_3^{(\beta_0)}/(2d_0)$; the leading term is body-independent and the body first acts at order $\lambda^2$.

For $d_0(h,h')>0$: $\alpha_2^{(\beta_0)}=\alpha_2^{(0)}-\operatorname{Im}\langle\chi\vert B_{\beta_0}\tilde D^2\vert\chi\rangle/(2d_0)$, where $\alpha_2^{(0)}=-\operatorname{Im}\langle\chi\vert K_{h'}\tilde D^2\vert\chi\rangle/(2d_0)$ is the body-free value.

Qubit example ($\mathcal H_c=\mathbb C^2$, $\chi=\lvert0\rangle$, $K_{h_i}=i\,X$ with $X=\sigma_x+\sigma_z$, $B_\beta=\beta\sigma_y$): $c_3^{(\beta_0)}(h_i,h_j)=2\beta_0(i-j)^2$, so $W^{(\beta_0)}(h_i,h_j;\lambda)=1-(i-j)^2\lambda^2+2\beta_0(i-j)^2\lambda^3+O(\lambda^4)$.

Same qubit example, as $\lambda\to0^+$: $\alpha_2^{(\beta_0)}(h_i,h_j)=-\beta_0\lvert i-j\rvert$ and $\alpha^{(\beta_0)}(h_i,h_j;\lambda)=\lambda\lvert i-j\rvert\,(1-\beta_0\lambda)+O(\lambda^3)$: to this order the body rescales all probe distances by the common factor $1-\beta_0\lambda$.

Contrast $B_\beta=\beta X$, which commutes with every $K_{h_i}$: $W^{(\beta_0)}(h_i,h_j;\lambda)=1-\tfrac12\sin^2\bigl(\sqrt2\,(i-j)\lambda\bigr)$ exactly, for every $\beta_0$ and every $\lambda$, so the body has no effect.

definitions.name: Probe: the object p forming the part A = {p}
Witness data of the probe in the presence of the body at β₀
Difference of two probe record operators, D = K_h − K_h'
Centered difference, D̃ = D − ⟨D⟩ with the expectation taken in χ
Third-order coefficient in λ of the witness data, with the body at β₀

open_issues: In general the body-free coefficient c₃⁽⁰⁾ = Im⟨χ|K_h' D̃²|χ⟩ is nonzero, so the body-free angle already has a λ² term; in the qubit example it vanishes, so there the third-order coefficient consists only of the body part.

The condition of item 2 (commuting records) is sufficient for exact body-independence, not necessary; at order λ³ the body term already vanishes when ⟨χ|[B_β₀, D̃²]|χ⟩ = 0, and necessary conditions were not studied.

In the qubit example it is not determined whether the uniform rescaling of the distances persists beyond order λ²; large λ, bodies in superposition, the dependence on a probe–body distance and the relation to the cost L are out of scope.

consistency_checks.check: B_β₀ = 0: (6.6) reduces to (5.6), the λ² coefficient of (6.9) is −Var_χ(K_h − K_h') as in (5.8)–(5.9), and the leading term of (6.12) gives α/λ → d₀ as in (5.10).
B_β₀ = β₀ times the identity: (6.7) gives no effect exactly, and at third order (6.11) agrees independently, since Im⟨β₀ D̃²⟩ = β₀ Im⟨D̃²⟩ = 0 for the self-adjoint D̃².
Qubit example with B_β = βX: the body part of (6.11) is β₀(i−j)² Im⟨3X − 2X²⟩ = 0, consistent with the exact no-effect statement (6.16) from item 2.
